items.headline: Small model or big model?
items.hook: Bigger is not always better. It depends on the job.
points: Two kinds of model, two sets of trade-offs.
items.ask: Would you pick a smaller, cheaper model if it did the job?
items.summary: Two kinds of model, two sets of trade-offs. Swipe for the comparison.
checks: written and reviewed in this project
includes the reminder not to paste customer or company data where data is involved

left.head: Smaller model
items: Usually cheaper and faster to run
Can sometimes run on a laptop
May be weaker on hard tasks
Can be trained to imitate a larger one (distillation)

right.head: Bigger model
items: Often more capable on hard tasks
Not always necessary for simple work
